Hi Laura — quick technical notes to address your procurement questions:

1) Invoice cadence / consolidation: Azure Marketplace Private Offers can be invoiced at the azure billing account level. We will work with your ARM billing admin to set the Marketplace subscription under the correct billing profile so invoices aggregate to your FinEdge, Inc. legal entity. There may be line-level detail per marketplace subscription, but we can provide a mapping file to help your AP match lines to internal GL codes.

2) Subscription IDs: the migration will create a new Marketplace-backed subscription object in Azure. We typically provide a reconciliation table (old_subscription_id -> marketplace_subscription_id) and a short script your billing system can run to map IDs during the first invoice cycle. We include that reconciliation deliverable as part of the migration packet.

3) Discounts / credits: commit discounts in Marketplace are implemented on the offer level and will reflect as a credit on the invoice. Refunds follow Microsoft’s marketplace policies; in practice, mechanics are similar but there are timing differences around proration. We'll document the edge cases for cancellations and credits in the final offer terms.

Action plan I propose:
- Week 1: finalize SKU mapping (we incorporate FinEdge GLs) and produce reconciliation table.
- Week 2: Draft Private Offer (Redwood to create) + DocuSign routing for FinEdge PO sign-off.
- Week 3: Sandbox cutover (we provision a test Marketplace subscription) and run reconciliation cycle.

I'll attach a short reconciliation template and a checklist in the follow-up (uploading to the shared Drive link). If it's helpful, we can also run a 30-min technical walkthrough with your ARM billing admin.

-Karthik
